qs: The scales in each scenario are identical. What is causing the pointer to change direction?
A different scale is being used
The dial is broken
The weight decreasing in mass
The weight increasing in mass
The time is different

The pointer changes by 90° for every 5kg that are added. In the first scenario it has rotated 90° clockwise as 5kgs is being suspended from it. In the second scenario the pointer has rotated 180° from its starting position, or 90° from the previous scenario and this is holding a 10kg weight. The last scenario it has rotated another 90° so we can assume that the weight added is more than 5kg, and more than 10 kg, and is probably 15kg. So the pointer changes direction as the weight increases.
What will happen in the scenario depicted if the ropes are released?
The weights will lift up
One weight will rise above the other
Both weights will rise to the same height
The ropes will snap
The weights will remain stationary
The ropes are being held up, so as soon as they are released they will fall towards the floor due to gravity. This will not have any effect on the weights.
The crates each contain 10 kilos of the contents depicted. If they are released at the same time, which crate will reach the ground first?
Rocks
Wood
Feathers
Rocks and Wood
All at the same time

The crates all have the same mass and shape and have the same distance to travel to reach the floor. Gravity will affect each of them equally. the contents of the crates do not matter. Therefore, as all the conditions are the same, the crates will all reach the ground at the same time.
Where will the water start to pool in the empty vessel depicted?
The handle
The sides of the beaker
The bottom of the beaker
The beaker will block the tap
The water will pour out the spout of the beaker when it is full

Water is a liquid, and like gases, is considered a fluid. A fluid is able to take on the shape of its container, in this case the beaker. Therefore, the water, which is dripping in to the cup, will be pulled down by gravity to the bottom of the beaker where it will start to pool, not the handle nor the sides.
Where on the lever will the least force be required to pull it down?
The base
The handle
Does not matter
It is not possible to move the lever
Two people will provide more strength to pull the lever

This is a question of fulcrums. The greater the distance from the point where the force is being applied to the fulcrum (pivot point) - the point which the lever hinges on) – the less force is required to move an object of the same mass by the same distance. In this case, the handle of the lever is the best place to apply the least amount of force possible to pull the lever down.
How many rotations does Cog B perform for every full rotation of Cog A?

The key difference here is in the circumference of the two cogs. Cog A is 10cm in circumference, which is twice as much as Cog B; 5cm. As Cog A and Cog B are interlocked, by the time Cog A has performed one rotation of 10cm, Cog B of 5cm, must have also rotated twice.
Cog A rotates clockwise by one revolution. In which direction would Cog D move and how many revolutions would it perform?
Clockwise once
Clockwise twice
Neither
Anticlockwise once
Anticlockwise twice

When one cog rotates, any directly interlocked will rotate in the opposite direction. Hence, if Cog A rotates clockwise, then B must go anti clockwise, then C clockwise again, and lastly, D anticlockwise. Ignoring all numbers except for those of Cog A and Cog D, we can see that the circumference of A is twice that of D. Therefore, for every 20cm Cog A rotates, Cog D must also do the same as the two are linked, which results in two rotations, due to Cog D having a circumference of 10cm.
How many rotations does Cog B perform for every one rotation of Cog A?
This is a simplified version of the previous question. Considering the circumferences of the two cogs, Cog B performs one and a quarter rotations for every rotation of Cog A.
In which direction are the energetic molecules moving?
To the top
To the bottom
Every direction
To the right
To the left
All the molecules are not stationary as stated in the question. There doesn’t appear to be any general direction that they are all moving towards.
The same type of rope is used in each pulley system. In which scenario would it be easiest to hoist up the weight using the rope and pulley?
A
B
C
A or B
All scenarios equally

The rope is still looped over the pulley system. The length of the rope is the only variable that changes in the three scenarios; A, B and C. This has no effect on how easy or difficult it would be to lift the weight off the ground.
Which of these three spanners would it be the easiest to LOOSEN the nut with?
A
B
C
A and C
All spanners are equally easy for the task

The length of the spanner is the only variable that changes in the three scenarios; A, B and C. As mentioned earlier, in question 5, the longer the distance to the point at which the pivoting occurs, the easier it is to perform the action. In this case, C would be the best spanner to loosen the nut with.
A, B, C and D are all glassware connected via a glass tube and held upright. Water is poured into where the arrow is indicated. In which object would the water level be the highest?
A
B
C
D
The water level would be the same across all glassware

Similar to question 4. Water is a liquid, and like gases, is considered a fluid. A fluid is able to take on the shape of its container. Therefore, the water, which is poured into the glass tube, will occupy any available space. As all of the glassware is connected, the water will rise to the same level in each of the ‘objects’.
A lead object is added to each beaker. Which tank will the water level rise the most when the object is added to it?
A
B
C
A and C
They will all rise by the same amount

The starting water level is different in each beaker. The object added to each beaker is the same. The object will therefore have the same volume, so when placed in the beakers, it will displace the same amount of water, regardless of the starting level. As each of the beakers are the same, the water level will rise by the same amount.

25 kg of mass is placed upon the point indicated by the arrow. The distance between point A and the 25 kg mass is distance X. Y is half the distance of X. At which point would you place a 50 kg mass to balance the see-saw?
A
B
C
X
Anywhere on the left-hand side of the see-saw

A 50kg mass is twice that of a 25kg mass. To make the two balance when they are placed either side of a pivot, the heavier 50kg mass must be placed half the distance from the pivot. If Y is half of distance X, then the 50kg mass must be placed at position B.
Which of the following constructions would you most expect to be knocked down when the same force is applied to the point marked ‘x’?
A
B
C
D
E

Stability of an object is dependent on its centre of gravity. An object with a lower centre of gravity is more stable. The centre of gravity depends on the object’s shape. Stability is also dependent on how close the centre of gravity is to a point from which it can be knocked over. A is the least stable because it has one of the highest centres of gravity out of all the constructions and its centre of gravity is close to its edge, from where it can be knocked over. B, C and E are much wider and more would be required to topple them.

Ice is less dense than water, as such it floats on the surface partially submerged. An ice cube, of 6 cm3 and two discs of ice, of 4 cm3 each. By what volume will the water level rise as soon as the ice has been placed in the tank?
6 cm3
10 cm3
14 cm3
Less than 14 cm3
More than 14 cm3

Similar to question 13, but with a caveat. The volume of the ice is given as 14cm3, but ice does not fully submerge in the water, instead it floats on top, so not all of the volume of ice displaces water, so the water level will not rise by 14cm3 but by slightly less. How much exactly is difficult to tell, but there is an option, D, to cover any measurements below 14cm3.
A wheelbarrow is being pushed up a hill. Which hill gradient would it be easiest for the wheelbarrow to be pushed up?
The gradient doesn’t matter

As the hill gradient approaches 90° the person pushing the wheelbarrow is lifting it against the force of gravity. So, having no gradient, or even pushing a wheelbarrow down a hill, would require less force. The smallest gradient, 5°, is therefore the easiest.
As the crane moves the weight on the hook in the direction of the arrow how could the crane increase its stability to prevent it falling over?
Decrease the mass of the counterweight
Bring the counterweight closer to the tower of the crane
Increase the mass of the weight
Increase the height of the crane
None of the above

All of the options given would actually make the crane less stable. As the weight on the hook moves away from the crane, the crane’s chances of falling over in that direction increase, unless something is done to counter that. The counterweight acts as a balance. Bringing it closer to the crane as the weight on the hook moves away would have a destabilising effect. The same goes for decreasing the mass of the counterweight. Increasing the height of the crane would make its centre of gravity even higher, which would reduce its stability. The only answer option therefore is E, which is to do none of the recommendations of A – D.

Two people are pushing against a wall. They are pushing with an equal force in opposite directions exactly at the height where their hands are. In which direction is the wall most likely to fall if it remains in one piece?
Towards the man
Towards the boy
The wall will crumble on the spot it stands
The wall will not fall down
The top will fall towards the man, the middle will fall towards the boy

They are both pushing with an equal force, but the man is pushing at a point higher up the wall than the boy. The distance to the ground is greater, therefore if the same force was applied by the man as the boy, the effect would be a greater force where the man is pushing. Hence, if the wall were to topple as one piece it would do so in the direction of the boy.
The tap has a hole in the top so that when the end is blocked water will flow out of the hole. What would happen to the jet of water from the hole if the hole was made narrower?
The jet of water will reach a lower height and be narrower
The jet of water will reach a lower height and be wider
The jet of water will reach a greater height and be narrower
The jet of water will reach a greater height and be wider
The jet of water will remain the same

As the hole is made narrower, the water being pushed through it is still the same, so it will be at a higher pressure. This will force the water into a narrower stream which will reach a greater height.
